title: The Song Before the Hard Choice

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE I: SONGS, CHANTS, SPEECHES AND WELCOMES (LCA-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola sings, chants and speaks for itself: welcoming a new leader, wishing travelers luck, greeting newcomers and newborns, rallying for hard work, standing up for each other, and arguing about who gets the next verse.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A villager must decide whether to leave Isola to look after a relative far away: sing for them, or just listen.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Word has come that (subject)'s aunt, who lives on an island far to the south, is old and alone. (subject) could go and look after her, but it would mean leaving Isola for a long time, maybe for good. (subject.He/she) has not slept for worrying about it. (friend) thinks the village should do something. What should they do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The village sings the choosing song, the one that says whatever you decide, you are still ours. (subject) listens with (subject.his/her) head down. Afterwards, (subject.he/she) says (subject.he/she) still does not know what to do. But (subject.he/she) is not afraid of deciding anymore.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) sits with (subject) all evening by the fire and listens while (subject.he/she) talks it through, again and again. (friend) gives no advice at all. By morning, (subject) has decided to stay a little longer and send gifts south with the next traders. (subject.He/she) may change (subject.his/her) mind. That is allowed.
